title: Welcome to Zenith
content:
# Welcome to Zenith

Zenith is a powerful script execution environment with a custom Lua API. Built by a team of experienced developers and trusted by over **33,000 users**. You will never use another script executor with as much care and attention to detail as Zenith.

If you're viewing this page, you may be unfortunately experiencing difficulty using Zenith or wish to learn more. Please navigate around and use the search bar to find a suitable article for any issues you're having.

If these articles fail to help, you are welcome to create a support ticket to get direct one-on-one support from our expert Zenith support team (constantly rated #1 support experience!).

This video is a quick introduction to setting up Zenith and how to get started if you're new:

title: Executing Scripts with Zenith
content:
# Executing Scripts with Zenith

The Executor page is where you write and run your Lua scripts, as well as attach to Roblox.

If you've skipped or forgotten how to use the Executor page, navigate to Settings and click **Restart Tutorial** for a quick overview.

Using Zenith is straightforward:
1. Join a Roblox game, any game you would like is fine
2. Click **Attach** in Zenith, wait for it to finish injecting/attaching (top left of the interface will say "Attached" when complete)
3. Paste your script and click the **Execute** button

That's it! You can run any script you'd like.

**Note:** If [setting:errorSpoofing] is enabled, script errors appear in Zenith's console instead of Roblox's F9 console. This helps avoid detection in games with anti-cheat.

title: Using Multi-Instance
content:
# Using Multi-Instance

Enable [setting:multiInstance] to attach to multiple Roblox instances simultaneously.

**Important:** Enable this **BEFORE** opening any games.

## How to Use

1. Enable [setting:multiInstance]
2. Launch multiple Roblox instances
3. Click **Attach** (now labeled "Select Process")
4. Choose which processes to attach to

## Multi-Selection

Use **Ctrl+Click** in the process selection dialog to select multiple processes and execute the same script across all of them.

**Important:** If you're new, please don't forget to use different Roblox accounts for each instance to avoid disconnection issues. Roblox only allows one session per account at a time.

title: Using Auto-Attach
content:
# Using Auto-Attach

Auto-Attach automatically connects Zenith to Roblox when detected.

## Setup

1. Enable [setting:autoAttach]
2. Set [setting:autoAttachDelay] (recommended: 5 seconds)

## How It Works

When enabled, Zenith will:
1. Monitor for Roblox processes
2. Wait for the configured delay
3. Automatically attach to the game
4. Notify you of success or failure

The delay gives Roblox time to fully initialize before attachment, preventing connection issues.

title: Working with Tabs
content:
# Working with Tabs

Zenith supports multiple editor tabs for organizing scripts and improving workflow.

## Creating Tabs

- Click the **+** button next to existing tabs
- Press **Ctrl+T**

## Managing Tabs

- **Switch tabs**: Click tab headers
- **Close tabs**: Click the X button or press **Ctrl+W**
- **Rename tabs**: Right-click → "Rename"
- **Reorder tabs**: Drag and drop tab headers
- **Split view**: Right-click → "Open in Split View"
- **Quick management**: Press **Ctrl+P** to use the Command Palette, you can create, close, and switch tabs really quickly with this feature!

## Tab Persistence

Tabs are automatically saved. Close Zenith anytime and resume exactly where you left off. No more lost scripts!

title: Using the Script Hub
content:
# Using the Script Hub

The Script Hub provides access to community scripts via ScriptBlox.

Before you are given access, we show you a warning. These scripts are created and shared by the ScriptBlox community, not Zenith. We do not review or endorse these scripts. 

You are welcome to run and try any of these scripts with the knowledge that Zenith does not endorse, verify, review, or provide these scripts for you. They are provided by ScriptBlox exclusively (and their community).

title: Custom Themes
content:

One unique and fun feature is the ability to customize your UI however you want!

Navigate to [setting:theme] to create, import, or use pre-set themes we provide.

We regularly host theme contests on our Discord server where users can submit and share their custom themes with the community for prizes. Join our Discord to participate and download community-created themes!

title: Script Not Executing
content:
# Script Not Executing

Scripts not running is annoying, but usually easy to fix. Follow these steps:

## Check Attachment Status

Ensure Zenith is actually attached to the game:
1. Look for the attachment indicator (it should say "Attached" in the top left)
2. If not attached, click the **Attach** button and wait for it to complete.

## Console Errors

Check either Zenith's output console or the game's developer console (press **F9 in-game**) for any error messages. You can use this to gauge whether or not it was the script or Zenith itself that caused the issue. These provide clues about what went wrong.

If it is still not working, try the following:

## Use the Internal Interface
1. Enable [setting:internalInterface]
2. Set a keybind for [setting:internalKeybind]
3. In-game, press the keybind to open Zenith's internal interface
4. Execute the script from there

The issue could be related to the external interface not communicating properly with the game.

title: Connection Errors
content:
# Connection Errors

If you're experiencing connection issues with Zenith, here's how to resolve them.

Most connection issues occur because your ISP (internet provider) may be blocking Zenith's websites. You can resolve this by using WARP via one.one.one.one or by using a VPN service to bypass these restrictions.

The most common country with this issue is Russia, but it can happen anywhere. It is usually very easy to fix.

You can also ensure your firewall isn't causing issues with Zenith.

title: How do I update Zenith?
content:
# How do I update Zenith?

Zenith includes an automatic update system.

## Automatic Updates

Zenith checks for updates on startup:
1. You'll see a notification when updates are available
2. Zenith automatically downloads new files and either restarts or continues running based on the update type

## Update Issues

If updates fail:
- Check your internet connection
- Ensure firewall/antivirus isn't blocking Zenith
- Use Cloudflare WARP (one.one.one.one) to bypass ISP restrictions or use a VPN
- Redownload the latest **PACKAGED** version from zenith.win/user/dashboard

title: Is my data safe?
content:
# Is my data safe?

In a nutshell: **Absolutely. Yes.**

We store as little data as possible to allow our product to work.

From our site: **"We collect minimal data on our users as we value their privacy. The main data we collect is your Zenith account username, a strongly-protected (hashed & salted) variant of your password, and your email address. Please review our Privacy Policy for more details!"**

You can review our Privacy Policy: zenith.win/privacy-policy

We don't touch your scripts (they're only ever stored locally on your device), your login credentials are fully encrypted during transmission, and we follow industry-standard security practices.

We will **never** collect your script content, and we have **zero** telemetry or tracking of any kind - we don't even know your Roblox username!

**Note:** Scripts that use online services (e.g., does some sort of authentication) may send data to third-party servers. This is entirely separate from Zenith and is controlled by the script author, not us. Always review scripts before executing them if possible.

We trust you have already been lectured on privacy and security, and with great power comes great responsibility! Don't just run any script you find online without reviewing it first, or atleast reading about what it does.

title: Fixing Injection Issues
content:
# Fixing Injection/Attaching Issues

If Zenith won't inject/attach into Roblox, follow these troubleshooting steps in order.

**Note:** Every issue has a solution. Follow each step carefully for best results.

## Your Zenith Installation Path (IMPORTANT)
**YOUR ZENITH LOCATION:** `ZENITH_INSTALL`

You will need this path for this guide. Make sure to use **THIS path**, not anything else.

## 1. Delete Corrupted Files

Anti-virus software may corrupt Zenith's files even when disabled. Delete the `bin` folder and `Zenith-Module.dll` where the Zenith installation path is, then continue with the next step.

## 2. Exclude Zenith from Antivirus

Add a **permanent exclusion** instead of temporarily disabling anti-virus.

Let's begin by you pressing this button below to open Windows Security, then follow the steps:

[button-defender:Open Windows Security]

1. Click **Manage settings** under **"Virus & threat protection settings"**
2. Scroll to **Exclusions** → **Add or remove exclusions**
3. Click **Add an exclusion** → **Folder**
4. Select your Zenith folder: `ZENITH_INSTALL` (shown in Step 1)

**IMPORTANT**: Make sure to exclude the **entire Zenith folder**, not just specific files.
**IMPORTANT**: Do NOT exclude only `Zenith.exe` - this will NOT work.
**IMPORTANT**: If you use third-party antivirus software (Norton, Malwarebytes, McAfee, G Data, etc.), add the same exclusion there as well, research how to add folder exclusions for Zenith.

## 3. Restart Zenith

Close and restart Zenith to regenerate files with antivirus excluded.

## 4. Verify LIVE Roblox Version

Zenith only works with LIVE Roblox, not Beta or other channels.

Download the latest LIVE version from WEAO: rdd.weao.gg → select "Download Latest Version" → unzip the folder and run RobloxPlayerBeta.exe.

To learn more about Roblox channels, read this article: [article:LIVE vs Other Roblox Versions].

## 5. Attach Before Joining

Open Zenith and attach **BEFORE** joining a Roblox game. If this works, you're done!

**Still not working?** Restart your PC and try all steps again. If issues persist, create a support ticket via Discord (find the link in Settings).

title: Game Crashes When Executing Scripts
content:
# Game Crashes When Executing Scripts

If Roblox crashes when you execute scripts, follow these steps.

## 1. Reset Exploit Protection Settings

1. Go to Windows Security → App and Browser Control
2. Open Exploit Protection Settings
3. Set all options to "Use default (on)"

**This fixes most crashes - try this first!**

## 2. Reinstall Roblox Fresh

1. Press Windows + R, type `%localappdata%`
2. Delete the Roblox folder
3. Download a fresh copy from roblox.com/download

## 3. Disable Real-Time Protection

1. Turn off anti-tamper and real-time protection in Windows Security
2. Reinstall Zenith from the packaged zip

## 4. Test with Different Script

Try executing a simple script like Infinite Yield to isolate the issue.

title: Understanding HWID Resets
content:
# Understanding HWID Resets

HWID (Hardware ID) errors occur when your Zenith account is used across multiple computers too quickly.

## IMPORTANT: Two Different Types of HWID

This article is about **Zenith HWID** - the hardware lock on your Zenith account. This is different from **Script HWID**, which some paid scripts use.

**Zenith HWID:**
- Tied to your Zenith account and subscription
- Prevents your account from being used on multiple PCs
- Affects your ability to **login and use Zenith itself**

**Script HWID:**
- Used by individual paid scripts for their own copy protection
- Completely separate from Zenith
- Affects your ability to **run that specific script in-game**

**How to tell which HWID issue you have:**
- ✓ **Can't login to Zenith or getting HWID errors before attaching?** → Zenith HWID issue (this article applies)
- ✓ **Getting kicked from game with "HWID Mismatch" error?** → Script HWID issue (contact the script developer, not Zenith support)

## Reset Policy

You get **TWO automatic HWID resets every 24 hours** (non-stacking).

## Why This Happens

This protection prevents account sharing, which violates our terms of service.

## How to Resolve

1. Change your account password immediately
2. If using someone else's account, return it to the rightful owner
3. Wait 24 hours before logging in again

## Important

We will **NOT manually reset** your HWID. The automatic reset system is your only option.

Account sharing is prohibited and may result in license termination.

title: What Happens During Downtime

Occasionally, Zenith needs maintenance or updates. This can be due to server issues, major game updates, or emergency fixes.

## Typical Downtime

Most downtime lasts less than 24 hours. In rare cases, it may take 1-3 days for major updates. We strive to minimize downtime and restore service as quickly as possible.

You receive full time compensation for any downtime. Your subscription is automatically extended by the downtime duration. Additionally, we may offer bonus time as goodwill.

Check Discord announcements for real-time status updates and estimated return times. Alternatively, you can simply open Zenith during downtime to see a status message.

**Don't worry** - downtime is temporary and you won't lose any paid time.

title: Fixing Time Synchronization Errors
content:
# Fixing Time Synchronization Errors

"Time check failed" means your system time isn't synchronized properly.

## Fix 1: Synchronize Time

1. Open Windows Settings → Time & Date
2. Click "Synchronize now"
3. Try running Zenith again

## Fix 2: Reconfigure Time Service

Open Command Prompt as administrator and run:

```
w32tm /config /manualpeerlist:"pool.ntp.org" /syncfromflags:manual /update
net stop w32time
net start w32time
w32tm /resync /force
```

Then run Zenith as administrator.

## Fix 3: Use VPN

If you're in a region with restricted access, try using:
- Cloudflare WARP (one.one.one.one)
- ProtonVPN (protonvpn.com)

This usually fixes time-related initialization errors.

title: Roblox Won't Open After Injection

title: Using the VSCode Extension
content:
# Using the VSCode Extension

Zenith offers an official VSCode (Visual Studio Code) extension that lets you execute scripts directly from your editor without switching windows.

## What is the VSCode Extension?

The Zenith VSCode extension allows you to:
- Execute scripts directly from VSCode
- Keep your code in the familiar VSCode editor environment
- Eliminate context switching between VSCode and Zenith's UI
- Leverage VSCode's powerful features (IntelliSense, syntax highlighting, extensions)

## Getting the Extension

### Automatic Notification

If you have VSCode running while using Zenith, you'll see a one-time popup notification offering to install the extension. Click "Get Extension" to open it directly in VSCode.

### Manual Installation

If you missed the popup:

1. Open VSCode
2. Go to Extensions (Ctrl+Shift+X)
3. Search for "Zenith"
4. Install the extension by ZenithSoftware (ID: `ZenithSoftware.zenith-vsc`)

Or visit: marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ZenithSoftware.zenith-vsc

## How It Works

Once installed, you can execute your Lua scripts from VSCode while Zenith handles the injection and execution in the background. Your workflow stays in one place.

**Note:** Zenith must be running and attached to Roblox for the extension to execute scripts.

title: LIVE vs Other Roblox Versions
content:
# LIVE vs Other Roblox Versions/Channels

Zenith only works with the **LIVE (production) version/channel** of Roblox, not Beta or other versions.

In some cases, users may unknowingly be on an older or incorrect version of Roblox that prevents Zenith from injecting properly. This article helps you ensure you're on the correct version.

## Why am I not on LIVE?

Roblox offers multiple release channels, and you may not be on the LIVE channel by default. Zenith typically will let you know if you're not on LIVE when injection fails. It is entirely random, and there is no set reason why some users end up on another channel.

## Why LIVE is Required

Zenith's injection mechanism is specifically designed for the LIVE channel. Other versions have different binary structures that break compatibility, causing injection failures.

## Checking Your Roblox Version

The easiest way to ensure you're on LIVE is to use Zenith's built-in Force Live feature:

1. Go to **Settings**
2. Search for "Force Live"
3. Click "Force Live" option
4. Follow the dialog to check and update your version

## What Force Live Does

The Force Live feature:
- Detects your current Roblox version (supports standard Roblox, Bloxstrap, and Fishstrap)
- Checks if you're on the LIVE channel
- Downloads and installs the latest LIVE version if needed
- Sets your Windows registry to keep you on LIVE

## Manual Method

If you prefer to install manually, or the Force Live method fails:

1. Visit rdd.weao.gg
2. Select "Download Latest Version"
3. Unzip the entire folder to a new location, then run `RobloxPlayerBeta.exe`
4. Attach Zenith after Roblox is running

## Common Issues

**"Injection failed" or "Timeout"**: Often caused by being on Beta version instead of LIVE. Use Force Live to fix this.

**Note:** Always ensure you're on LIVE before attempting to inject Zenith. We will not support other Roblox versions.

title: Understanding Error Spoofing
content:
# Understanding Error Spoofing

Error Spoofing is an anti-detection feature that redirects script errors from the in-game console to Zenith's UI.

## What is Error Spoofing?

When enabled, Error Spoofing:
- Intercepts runtime errors from your executed scripts
- Redirects them to Zenith's Output Console (bottom panel)
- Prevents errors from appearing in Roblox's F9 developer console

![Error Spoofing Demo](/help-images/error-spoofing-overview.png)

## Why Use It?

**Anti-Cheat Evasion**: Many anti-cheat systems monitor the in-game console for suspicious errors or output. By keeping errors out of the F9 console, you reduce detection risk.

**Benefits:**
- In-game console stays clean (appears normal)
- You still see all errors in Zenith's UI
- Helps avoid console-based anti-cheat detection
- Also easier to view errors in one place

## How to Enable/Disable

Toggle [setting:errorSpoofing] to enable or disable this feature.

## Where Errors Appear

**Without Error Spoofing:**
- Errors show in Roblox's F9 developer console (in-game)

**With Error Spoofing:**
- Errors show in Zenith's Output Console (bottom panel of Executor page)
- Output from `printconsole()` also appears here

## When to Use It

Enable Error Spoofing when:
- Playing on servers with strict anti-cheat
- Wanting to avoid detection through console monitoring
- Testing scripts that might produce errors

**Note:** Error Spoofing requires Zenith to be attached to Roblox to work.

title: Managing Scripts and Files
content:
# Managing Scripts and Files

Zenith provides a complete file management system for organizing your scripts.

## Your File Storage Locations

- **Scripts (NOT TABS):** `%APPDATA%\Zenith\Scripts`
- **AutoExec files:** `%APPDATA%\Zenith\AutoExec`
- **Workspace files:** `%APPDATA%\Zenith\Workspace`

## Root Folders

The three aforementioned folders serve different purposes:

**Scripts Folder:**
- Your general script storage, like a "Documents" folder for scripts - place any scripts you want here
- Organize with custom subfolders, do whatever you'd like with it
- Accessible from the right-side file list sidebar on the executor page. This is what makes this folder special - you can quickly open and edit any scripts here directly from Zenith

**AutoExec Folder:**
- These are scripts that run **automatically on injection** without needing to manually execute them
- **Note:** Only scripts in the **root AutoExec folder** (this means nothing inside a folder inside of AutoExec) run automatically
- Place scripts here to have them execute every time you attach Zenith or teleport in-game
- Ideal for auto-farming scripts you always want active, or utility scripts you enjoy using every session
- You can disable AutoExec in Settings if needed
- See [article:Using Auto-Execute] for more details

**Workspace Folder:**
- Scripts that run and use the filesystem functions will only ever write and read from here
- This serves as a sandboxed environment for scripts that need file access. this prevents scripts from accessing your entire filesystem unnecessarily
- For example, functions like `saveinstance`, `writefile`, `readfile`, etc. will only work within this folder. See function documentation for more details on filesystem functions.

On the executor page, you can quickly open the Scripts and AutoExec via the file list, you can left-click files to quickly open the file in your explorer, and simply click the file to open them in a new tab. Then, you can edit and save them to their respective locations.

title: Using the Command Palette
content:
# Using the Command Palette

The Command Palette is a powerful, searchable interface for quick access to all (and a few exclusive) Zenith features without leaving your keyboard.

## Opening the Command Palette

Press **Ctrl+P** to open the Command Palette from anywhere in Zenith.

![Command Palette Overview](/help-images/command-palette-overview.png)

## What You Can Do

The Command Palette organizes hundreds of commands into categories:

### Navigation Commands
- Go to Home, Executor, ScriptHub, Documentation, or Settings
- Quick navigation without clicking through the UI

### Execution Commands
- **Attach to Roblox** - Auto-detects available processes
- **Execute Script** - Run current script
- **Clear Editor** - Clear current tab
- **Open Script File** - Load scripts from disk
- **Save Script File** - Save current script
- **Kill All Processes** - Terminate all attached processes
- **Select All Processes** - For multi-instance execution
- **Execute All Tabs** - Run all tabs sequentially

### Tab Management
- **New Tab** - Create new script tab
- **Close Current Tab** - Close active tab
- **Close All Tabs** - Close all tabs
- **Close Other Tabs** - Close all except current
- **Switch to Tab** - Jump to any open tab by name

### Settings Control
Every setting in Zenith can be toggled or edited directly from the Command Palette. Yes, every single one.

### Documentation Lookup
Search and view function documentation inline without leaving the palette:
- Type any function name to see its documentation
- View parameters, return values, and examples
- Copy syntax and code snippets with one click

![Command Palette Inline Docs](/help-images/command-palette-inline.png)

## Searching and Filtering

The Command Palette uses intelligent fuzzy matching:
- Type partial words to find commands
- Searches titles, descriptions, and aliases
- Results ranked by relevance
- Highlights matching text in yellow

### Examples:
- **Type "exec"** → finds Execute Script, Execute All Tabs, Enable Auto Execute
- **Type "fps"** → finds Unlock FPS, FPS Cap Value
- **Type "tabs"** → quick tab navigation commands (you can also use "t1" (or "tab1"/just the number "1") for Tab 1, "t2" for Tab 2, etc.)

## Command History

The palette tracks your usage:

**Recent Commands:** Last 5 commands you executed

**Frequently Used:** Top 5 most-used commands with usage count badge (e.g., "5×")

**Pinned Commands:** Click the star icon ⭐ to pin your favorite commands to the top

**Clear History:** Use the "Clear history" button to reset tracking

## Quick Switch Mode

Press **Ctrl+P** while the palette is already open:
- Enters quick switch mode
- Press Ctrl+P repeatedly to cycle through commands
- Release Ctrl to execute the selected command
- Perfect for rapid command access

## Inline Documentation Viewer

When you select a documentation command:
- Full function reference opens in the palette
- Shows description, syntax, parameters, and examples
- Copy buttons for code snippets
- Press Escape or Back button to return to commands

## Opening Files Directly

Type **"open "** followed by a file path to open files:
```
open C:\Scripts\myscript.lua
```
The file loads directly into a new tab. It's hooked to Zenith and you can save changes back to disk, making it easy to work with external scripts.

## Keyboard Navigation

**Ctrl+P** - Open palette / Quick switch mode

**↑ ↓ Arrow Keys** - Navigate through commands

**Enter** - Execute selected command

**Escape** - Close palette or exit documentation

**Click ⭐** - Pin/unpin command

## Tips

- Pin your most-used commands for instant access
- Use aliases: "exe" for Executor, "sh" for ScriptHub, "?" for Documentation
- The palette remembers your frequently used commands
- Settings changes are instant - no need to close the palette
- Tab switching shows your current tab with a bullet point (•)

The Command Palette is designed to keep your hands on the keyboard and your workflow uninterrupted.

title: Keyboard Shortcuts Reference
content:
# Keyboard Shortcuts Reference

Quick reference for Zenith-specific keyboard shortcuts.

## Essential Shortcuts

**Ctrl+P** - Open Command Palette (see [article:Using the Command Palette] for full details)

**Ctrl+T** - New tab

**Ctrl+W** - Close current tab

**Ctrl+R** - Refresh Zenith application

**Escape** - Close modals, exit views, go back

## Tab Management

**Ctrl+T** - Create new tab

**Ctrl+W** - Close current tab

**Middle Mouse Click** - Close tab (click on tab header)

**Right-Click Tab** - Open context menu (Rename, Split View, etc.)

## Output Console

**Enter or Space** - Cycle console height (while hovering over resize handle)

Toggles between: 100px → 30% → 50% → Maximum height

## Execution

**Ctrl+Click** - Multi-select processes (in process selection dialog)

**Enter** - Execute focused button (when Execute/Attach/Clear button has focus)

## Settings

**Insert** - Internal Interface Keybind (default, customizable via [setting:internalKeybind])

## Editor Shortcuts

Zenith uses the Monaco editor. For a complete list of editor shortcuts, see: microsoft.github.io/monaco-editor/

Common shortcuts include Ctrl+/, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+K, Alt+Up/Down, and more.

## Command Palette

**Ctrl+P** gives you keyboard access to virtually everything in Zenith. See [article:Using the Command Palette] for complete details on:
- Navigation shortcuts
- Quick Switch Mode
- Settings control
- File operations
- Documentation lookup

## Disabling Editor Hints

If you were brought here from the editor hint overlay, you can disable it in [setting:showEditorHints].

The editor hints appear at the bottom of empty tabs to help new users discover essential shortcuts. Once you're familiar with Zenith's shortcuts, feel free to disable them for a cleaner interface.

title: Using the Internal Interface (In-Game UI)
content:
# Using the Internal Interface (In-Game UI)

The Internal Interface is a lightweight in-game overlay for fast script execution without alt-tabbing.

## How to Enable

1. Enable [setting:internalInterface]
2. Customize [setting:internalKeybind] (default: **Insert**)
3. Attach Zenith to Roblox
4. Press your keybind in-game

![Internal Interface Demo](/help-images/internal-gui-overview.png)

## What It Does

Execute scripts directly in-game without switching windows. Perfect for quick testing and rapid iteration during gameplay.

## Key Differences from Main GUI

**Has:**
- Fast script execution in-game
- Minimal UI overlay

**Doesn't Have:**
- Output console
- Tab management
- File operations
- Script Hub/Documentation
- Advanced editor features

**Important:** You must attach using the main GUI first. The Internal Interface only works on already-attached processes.

## When to Use It

**Internal Interface:** Quick script testing without leaving the game

**Main GUI:** Everything else (managing scripts, viewing errors, accessing features)

Disabled by default - enable via [setting:internalInterface].

title: Using Create LocalScript
content:
# Using Create LocalScript

The Create LocalScript setting is designed for legacy scripts that expect to run within a LocalScript instance.

## What It Does

When enabled, your executed scripts will run under a randomly-generated LocalScript in-game rather than directly in the environment.

## When to Use It

**Only enable this for legacy scripts** that specifically expect to be running within a LocalScript instance. Most modern scripts do not need this.

## How It Works

- Zenith creates a LocalScript with a randomly generated name
- Your code executes within that LocalScript context
- The LocalScript name is random and changes each execution

Enable via [setting:createLocalScript].

title: Using FPS Unlocker
content:
# Using FPS Unlocker

Control your in-game frame rate beyond Roblox's built-in limits.

## Roblox vs Zenith

**Roblox's FPS Unlocker:** 60-240 FPS only

**Zenith's FPS Unlocker:** 1 FPS to uncapped

## Why Use It

**Low FPS (1-30):** Reduce CPU/GPU usage for auto-farming or background running

**High FPS (240+):** Smoother gameplay and better performance

Enable [setting:unlockFPS] and set [setting:fpsCapValue] to control your frame rate.

title: Using Auto-Execute
content:
# Using Auto-Execute

Auto-Execute automatically runs scripts from your AutoExec folder when you attach to Roblox.

## How It Works

AutoExec scripts run **before the game's ReplicatedFirst**, making them fast and powerful. Your scripts execute immediately on attachment, before most game systems load.

## Setup

1. Place scripts in the **AutoExec** folder (`%APPDATA%\Zenith\AutoExec`)
2. Enable [setting:enableAutoExec]
3. Attach to Roblox - scripts run automatically

**Note:** Only scripts in the root AutoExec folder run automatically, not in subfolders. See [article:Managing Scripts and Files] for more about file organization.

## Use Cases

- Auto-farming scripts that need to run every session
- Utility scripts you always want active
- Game-specific configurations that load on join

Additionally, you can disable AutoExec temporarily via [setting:enableAutoExec] if needed. You can also run AutoExec scripts by running the script `runautoexec()` manually from the executor after attaching.

## Troubleshooting: Scripts Not Running

If your AutoExec scripts fail to run, the game may not be fully loaded yet. Add this line at the start:

```
if not game.IsLoaded then game.Loaded:Wait() end
print("AutoExec script loaded!")
```

This ensures the game is fully loaded before your script executes.
